reviews.summary: 以 IT 服务台报修系统为测试场景审阅 NocoBase3 基础框架。共审阅 4 个能力单元：复合授权与仓储写策略、数据库迁移/种子加载、应用内通知与收件箱接入、服务端路由类型表面。核心发现是授权与加载机制本身按声明可靠执行，失败主要来自应用侧配置（只读 action 写库、种子越界导入、通知入口缺失、容器类型未解析），框架侧存在若干文档/诊断改进点（自定义 handler 写授权警示、snapshot 覆盖边界、通知入口提醒）。工厂停在 needs-diagnosis，但不足以判定框架缺陷。

modules.scope: 复合资源定义/校验、数据库策略合成、仓储写操作的运行时拦截，以及自定义 handler 的授权边界。以工单 Comment 403 为观察点。

requirements.need: 工单各角色的写动作（评论/分派/解决/确认）在服务端被正确授权
requirements.responsibility: 复合资源定义校验 action 至少一个 grant；数据库策略按 collection 合成 CRUD；仓储写操作在 policy.update===false 时抛 WRITE_FORBIDDEN。
requirements.recommendedUsage: 写动作显式声明 .update(fields)；只读动作不得在执行时写库。
requirements.actualUsage: ticketComment 仅 .options(...)（resources.ts:99-105），但 addNote→transition 写 tickets，运行时返回 403。

requirements.need: 客户端可见动作与服务端判定一致，避免渲染必然被拒的按钮
requirements.responsibility: Authorization.snapshot 汇总 can() 允许的动作供客户端渲染。
requirements.recommendedUsage: 把有副作用的动作建模为写授权，客户端据此显示按钮。
requirements.actualUsage: snapshot 以 resolveConditions=false 求值，Comment 按钮可见但服务端 403。

requirements.need: 自定义 handler 绑定复合动作时的授权边界可诊断
requirements.responsibility: authorizeRepository 在集成期校验映射操作；guidance 说明自定义 handler 的授权责任。
requirements.recommendedUsage: 每个绑定 action 只含一个 data scope 且包含映射 CRUD；有工作流状态的动作用自定义 handler 并自行 withPolicy。
requirements.actualUsage: 应用把写操作放在映射为 read 的 action handler 中，403 报文不指出缺失的 operation。

requirementFit.reason: 授权模型能表达该场景，但只读动作写库导致核心评论能力在非 root 角色下不可用，需求达成受限。

usability.reason: 运行时拒绝正确，但 403 不含缺失 operation；guidance 未在自定义 handler 处给出显式警示。

agentFriendliness.reason: 文档展示了 update 授予与自定义 handler 规则，但缺少“handler 写库需要对应 update”这一直接检查点，Agent 易漏。

design.reason: 定义校验、策略合成与写拦截分层清晰，未授权写被硬性拒绝，安全边界可靠。

reliability.reason: 实现层在 policy.update===false 时确定性抛 WRITE_FORBIDDEN，避免越权写入。

findings.title: 未授权的仓储写入被运行时策略可靠拒绝
findings.detail: composeDatabasePolicies 对只读授予保留 update:false，resolveMutationNode 在该值为 false 时抛 WRITE_FORBIDDEN。工单 Comment 只授予读却写库，因此被一致拒绝，证明安全边界生效而非放行。
findings.impact: 框架在最坏情况下仍拒绝越权写入，不会因应用漏配授权而静默破坏数据。
findings.suggestedChange: 保持现状；可在拒绝信息中附带缺失的 operation 以改善诊断。

findings.title: 工单 Comment 对所有非 root 角色返回 403
findings.detail: ticketComment 以 ticketRead.options(...) 定义，只含读权限，但 handler 通过 transition→repository.updateOne 写 tickets 的 status 等字段，命中 policy.update===false 被拒。
findings.impact: 工程师无法记录处理过程、员工/服务台无法留言，核心业务动作在非 root 角色下完全不可用。
findings.suggestedChange: 为 ticketComment 增加 .update([...]) 授权，或把评论写入拆到独立的自定义 handler 并显式绑定策略。

findings.title: 自定义 handler 写操作的授权指引缺少显式警示与开发期校验
findings.detail: repository-routes.md 说明了自定义 handler 与映射 CRUD 的要求，但没有一句直接指出“handler 若写库，action 必须授予对应 update”，且框架只在集成期校验 Repository 路由，不校验自定义 handler 的实际写入。
findings.impact: Agent 容易把写操作放进只读 action，直到运行期才以通用 403 暴露，排查成本高。
findings.suggestedChange: 在自定义 handler 段落加入“handler 写库 ⇒ action 必须含 update grant”的显式规则，并在可能时于授权拒绝信息中标注缺失 operation。

diagnosis.trigger: 复合 action 的 handler 执行未在 action grants 中声明的写操作。
diagnosis.expected: 指引或开发期校验提前指出需要 update 授权。
diagnosis.actual: 仅运行期返回通用 403，指引未显式警示。
diagnosis.workaround: 为写动作显式 .update(fields)，或改用自定义 handler 并自行 withPolicy。
diagnosis.acceptance: 新增指引语句或拒绝信息包含缺失 operation，即可据此定位。

feedbackReview.reason: 停止诊断只允许单次只读调用；保留待定向复核的候选。

findings.title: snapshot() 可能显示服务端会拒绝的动作
findings.detail: Authorization.snapshot 以 resolveConditions=false 求值，注释却声称“客户端从不显示服务端拒绝的动作”。当 action 的 handler 执行超出声明 grants 的写操作时，snapshot 仍报告 permitted，造成客户端/服务端判定分歧。
findings.impact: 用户看到可点击的按钮却收到 403，体验与可预期性受损。
findings.suggestedChange: 收敛注释措辞，或在文档中说明 snapshot 仅覆盖声明层授权、不涵盖 handler 副作用。

diagnosis.trigger: action 声明与 handler 实际写入不一致时。
diagnosis.expected: 客户端可见动作与服务端允许动作一致。
diagnosis.actual: Comment 按钮可见但服务端 403。
diagnosis.workaround: 确保 action grants 覆盖 handler 的所有写入。
diagnosis.acceptance: 文档明确 snapshot 的覆盖边界，或对未解析条件给出保守结果。

feedbackReview.reason: 停止诊断只允许单次只读调用；保留待定向复核的候选。

findings.title: 种子文件越界相对导入导致种子加载失败
findings.detail: round-1 种子 import database/seed-data/service-desk.js，原生动态 import 无法解析 .js 路径，抛 ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND；最终快照的种子已改为自包含。
findings.impact: 种子与依赖它的 app-server 测试整体失败，阻塞启动。
findings.suggestedChange: 遵循 nocobase-db SKILL 的 self-contained 规则，种子不 import 目录外模块。

findings.title: 服务端路由容器解析触发 56 条 no-unsafe lint
findings.detail: round-4 中 file-routes.ts 的 app.container.resolve(authenticationToken) 被报 no-unsafe-assignment/call/member-access，全部是“类型无法解析”；后续为路由辅助函数显式标注 app: Application 后消除。
findings.impact: lint 失败阻断构建，且错误信息不直接指向类型解析根因。
findings.suggestedChange: 按 server-routes.md 示例显式标注 Application 类型并确保相关包类型可解析。

findings.title: 通知中心缺少导航/头部入口
findings.detail: 应用声明了 /inbox 路由但未声明 navigation，也未在 header 实现入口；verify-6 只能手输 URL 访问。app-client 已提供 navigation 元数据，声明即可进菜单。
findings.impact: 用户无法发现通知中心，通知能力形同虚设。
findings.suggestedChange: 在 /inbox 路由声明 navigation.title/icon，或在 header 增加带未读徽标的入口。

findings.title: verify-2 呈现未构建的空白 NocoBase 骨架
findings.detail: verify-2 验收时应用仅有 Home 导航，业务路由重定向、collections/roles/users/notifications API 全部 404；此后轮次恢复正常。该现象更像构建/环境未就绪，而非框架实现缺陷。
findings.impact: 一轮验收完全无效，浪费修复预算，但不足以推断框架缺陷。
findings.suggestedChange: 在验收前确保业务构建产物已生成并完成种子；由工厂流程校验。

findings.detail: SKILL 与 inbox-integration 明确“应用拥有页面与路由”，但未提醒还需提供导航/头部入口；应用据此只注册了路由而遗漏入口。

processNotes.author: implementer
processNotes.summary: Repaired the service-desk verification failures across rounds: made the permission-set seed self-contained so it loads outside the compiled seeds directory, made the application provider tolerate a runtime without the authorization plugin, stopped hard-coding the template package name in the sample-data source, and applied Prettier to the ticket-schema input so the repository-wide format check passes. All 224 logic tests pass and the exact factory format command exits 0. In the lint-repair round the server routes were re-pointed at the types that actually exist (shared error class in domain.ts, the base Application for the file plugin, ApiResponseObject instead of the missing ApiErrorResponse), the ticket pages were rewritten to derive loading instead of setting state in effects and to keep helpers out of component modules, the DataTable compiler and index-key warnings were resolved, and the ticket feature was given its English and Chinese translations. Full lint, format, typecheck, the 224 logic tests and the production build all pass. In the final round the landing page itself was the remaining defect: the service desk overview had been built on a separate /dashboard route while client/pages/home/index.tsx still returned the template onboarding placeholder, so a signed-in user saw no service desk UI. client/pages/home/index.tsx now renders the overview (moved from /dashboard), its ticket drawer is a :ticketId child of the / route, the duplicate /dashboard route and the onboarding capabilities/prompt-dialog/use-copy modules were removed, and the route and page tests were updated. All 224 tests, typecheck, scoped lint/format and the production build pass.

blockers.symptom: AppDatabaseTaskError: Database seeds failed for connection "main": Cannot find module '/workspace/database/seed-data/service-desk.js' imported from database/main/seeds/202611010002_service_desk_permission_sets.ts. The 'starts a fresh Default' and 'serves Users and API Keys' installed-server tests failed and the application could not start.
blockers.rootCause: Migrations and seeds are loaded with a bare native import from Node, so a relative './file.js' specifier is not rewritten to the '.ts' source that exists in development. The seed's shared permission-set data lived in database/seed-data, outside the compiled database/<connection>/seeds directory, so the specifier resolved nowhere.
blockers.resolution: Inlined the permission-set grant values into the seed file, which is now self-contained immutable history, and deleted database/seed-data. The composite grant shape is stored as plain PermissionGrant values referencing the composite resource id the boot-time model registers.

blockers.title: Application provider required the authorization plugin in every runtime
blockers.symptom: Error: Service "@nocobase/app/authorization" is not registered, thrown at server/service-desk/provider.ts:48 during ServiceDeskProvider.boot; tests/logic/app-server.test.ts > 'registers application-owned providers and routes from the runtime' failed.
blockers.rootCause: That template test resolves the application runtime with plugins set to an empty list, so the authorization plugin's service token is never registered. ServiceDeskProvider resolved authorizationToken unconditionally in both boot() and start().
blockers.resolution: Guard boot() and start() with container.has(authorizationToken) and skip declaring the permission model and scheduling the overdue scan when the plugin is absent; the normal application always registers it.

evidence.excerpt:
## Enforcement and limits

- Mount the middleware on every action of the named exposure. Using `'*'` is appropriate inside an isolated, owned router: the middleware ignores other repository names. A method of its repository with no mapping is denied, including methods added to the generated route later.
- The middleware reuses the request's existing authorization context or initializes one. Authentication is still the owning route's responsibility.
- Each bound action must declare exactly one data scope, compose grants on that collection only and contain the mapped CRUD operation. Multi-collection or same-collection multi-scope actions are rejected at integration time. Resource registration must precede router creation.
- One composite can be bound to several Repository exposures through separate middleware instances. Each mapping is checked at the action level. An exposure's actual collection and database connection must match the request constraint; this adapter currently supports the default connection only.
- Keep actions requiring workflow state, cross-record relationships, or side effects in custom handlers. Single-scope authorization does not prove that an operation needs no business validation. Quote editing/submission and delivery remain custom in the sales workflow.

evidence.observation: importTaskDefinition 用 pathToFileURL + __rewriteRelativeImportExtension 后原生 import；扩展名重写只作用于 task 文件自身 URL，不重写其内部相对 import。
loadSeedFile 读取源码后调用 importTaskDefinition 原生加载种子模块，种子内相对导入按原生解析。

evidence.excerpt:
The rules are absolute, because these files are history that has already run on other machines:

- **Self-contained.** Spell out every table, field, index, constraint and metadata operation in the file. Never import a Collection definition, model, registry or shared constant that keeps evolving — that silently changes both the behavior and the checksum of something already applied.
- **Immutable once merged.** Check with `git log -- <file>` if unsure. Before the branch is merged you may correct the file in place; after it, every change is a new, later file. Never hard-code a previous checksum to make an edited migration look untouched. Correcting it in place changes nothing on its own — it is recorded as executed, so a plain apply skips it and the database keeps the schema the old file produced. `pnpm nocobase db redo` rolls the latest batch back and applies it again.
- **The file name body matches `name`**, and the name is unique across every source in the application.
- **Declare `irreversible: true`** when there is no real reverse operation, instead of writing a `down()` that quietly does nothing.
- **A seed is idempotent**, keyed on a stable business value backed by a unique constraint, so a repeated run is a no-op — `upsertOne` is the direct way to express that. A seed context has no `builder` at all, and a seed has no rollback or truncate behavior.

evidence.observation: 说明迁移/种子回调的 container 仅允许白名单 token，并要求历史 schema 定义自包含而非委派给演进中的服务。
evidence.excerpt:
Migration callbacks and seed `run` also receive `container`, a `ServiceResolver` exposing `has(token)`, `resolve(token)`, and `resolveIfCreated(token)`. Application task runners wrap the application container with a token-identity allowlist; only `idGeneratorToken` from `@nocobase/app-server/id-generator` is currently allowed. Use `container.resolve(idGeneratorToken).generateString()` for string IDs or `.generate()` for numeric IDs. Disallowed tokens return false from `has` and throw from both resolution methods. The wrapper reuses application singleton instances and exposes no registration methods. Startup and CLI share the application factory in `server/app.ts`, which registers `IdGeneratorProvider`; CLI database commands call the application factory discovered from `rootDir/server/app.ts` (or `.js` in compiled applications), register its providers without booting or starting them, and use its database manager and migration contributions. They dispose the application and runtime scope after execution, including failure and cancellation. Keep the factory free of startup side effects; CLI does not call `app.start()` or trigger autoRun. Services must therefore be usable after provider registration; do not depend on later boot/start hooks. Direct application and database runners accept a `container` option. Without a source container, an allowed token returns false from `has`, undefined from `resolveIfCreated`, and a missing-service error from `resolve`. Standalone `@nocobase/db` runners accept an owner-supplied resolver; the application allowlist is enforced by `app-server`, including direct `createAppMigrator` and `createAppSeeder` calls.

Use the callback's `query` and `builder` for transactional database work. Services resolved from the container are application-scoped and are not automatically rebound to the migration or seed transaction. Keep historical schema definitions self-contained rather than delegating them to evolving application services.

Database commands load the runtime and application modules lazily from `server/runtime` and `server/app` below the application root, preferring `.ts` over `.js` when both exist. Module execution errors propagate without falling back to another file.

{"type":"tool_execution_end","toolCallId":"call_5bzmc9d5","toolName":"bash","result":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"agent-browser snapshot -i

# Pick the email/password refs out of the snapshot, then:
agent-browser fill @e3 "user@example.com"
agent-browser fill @e4 "hunter2"
agent-browser click @e5
agent-browser wait --url "**/dashboard"
agent-browser snapshot -i
```

Credentials in shell history are a leak. For anything sensitive, use the auth vault (see [references/authentication.md](references/authentication.md)):

```bash
agent-browser auth save my-app --url https://app.example.com/login \
  --username user@example.com --password-stdin
# (type password, Ctrl+D)

agent-browser auth login my-app    # fills + clicks, waits for form
```

If credentials live in an external vault, use a configured credential provider plugin instead of putting secrets in the command line:

```bash
agent-browser plugin add agent-browser-plugin-vault --name vault
agent-browser plugin list
agent-browser auth login my-app --credential-provider vault --item "My App"
agent-browser auth login my-app --credential-provider vault --item "My App" --url https://app.example.com/login --username-selector "#email" --password-selector "#password"
```

Plugins can also provide browser providers, launch mutators such as stealth setup, and arbitrary namespaced commands:

```bash
agent-browser --provider cloud-browser open https://example.com
agent-browser plugin run captcha captcha.solve --payload '{"siteKey":"...","url":"https://example.com"}'
```

`plugin run` is for `command.run` and custom capabilities. Core capabilities and protocol request types use their dedicated command paths.

### Persist session across runs

```bash
# Derive one stable id for this agent/worktree
SESSION="$(agent-browser session id --scope worktree --prefix my-app)"

# Pass the same id and restore request on every command
agent-browser --session "$SESSION" --restore open https://app.example.com
```

`--restore` with no value uses the current `--session` as the persistence key. Agent skills should prefer this over hand-built state file paths. Use `--restore-save auto` by default so a failed restore does not overwrite the previous known-good state. State is saved on close and also periodically while the browser is open (at most once per `AGENT_BROWSER_AUTOSAVE_INTERVAL_MS`, default 30000), so state survives even if the user closes the browser window by hand.

```bash
agent-browser --session "$SESSION" --restore --restore-check-text Dashboard open https://app.example.com
agent-browser --session "$SESSION" session info --json
```

### Extract data

```bash
# Structured snapshot (best for AI reasoning over page content)
agent-browser snapshot -i --json > page.json

# Targeted extraction with refs
agent-browser snapshot -i
agent-browser get text @e5
agent-browser get attr @e10 href

# Arbitrary shape via JavaScript
cat <<'EOF' | agent-browser eval --stdin
const rows = document.querySelectorAll("table tbody tr");
Array.from(rows).map(r => ({
  name: r.cells[0].innerText,
  price: r.cells[1].innerText,
}));
EOF
```

Prefer `eval --stdin` (heredoc) or `eval -b <base64>` for any JS with quotes or special characters. Inline `agent-browser eval "..."` works only for simple expressions.

### Screenshot

```bash
agent-browser screenshot                        # temp path, printed on stdout
agent-browser screenshot page.png               # specific path
agent-browser screenshot --full full.png        # full scroll height
agent-browser screenshot --annotate map.png     # numbered labels + legend keyed to snapshot refs
```

Headless Chromium screenshots hide native scrollbars for consistent image output. Pass `--hide-scrollbars false` when launching to keep native scrollbars visible.

`--annotate` is designed for multimodal models: each label `[N]` maps to ref `@eN`.

### Handle multiple pages via tabs

```bash
agent-browser tab                      # list open tabs (with stable tabId)
agent-browser tab new https://docs...  # open a new tab (and switch to it)
agent-browser tab t2                   # switch to tab t2
agent-browser tab close t2             # close tab t2
```

Stable `tabId`s mean `t2` points at the same tab across commands even when other tabs open or close. After switching, refs from a prior snapshot on a different tab no longer apply — re-snapshot. `tab list --json` also reports each tab's CDP `targetId`, accepted anywhere a tab ref is accepted; target ids stay stable across daemon restarts, unlike `t<N>` ids.

Switching has two special cases worth knowing:

- **Discarded tab (Chrome Memory Saver).** A backgrounded tab may have its renderer dropped. Switching to it reactivates the tab, which reloads the page and discards unsaved state (form input, scroll position). The switch result then includes `"revived": true`, so treat prior in-page state as gone and re-snapshot. Closing the active tab onto a discarded successor reports `"activeTabRevived": true` for the same reason.
- **Tab blocked by a dialog.** If the target tab has an open dialog (`confirm`/`prompt`, or `alert`/`beforeunload` under `--no-auto-dialog`) its renderer is paused, not discarded, so the switch leaves it untouched and reports `"dialogBlocked": true`. Resolve the dialog with `dialog accept`/`dialog dismiss` before interacting with the page.

### Run multiple browsers in parallel

Each `--session <name>` is an isolated browser with its own cookies, tabs, and refs. For agent skills, derive stable names with `agent-browser session id --scope worktree --prefix <skill>`. Useful for testing multi-user flows or parallel scraping:

```bash
agent-browser --session a open https://app.example.com
agent-browser --session b open https://app.example.com
agent-browser --session a fill @e1 "alice@test.com"
agent-browser --session b fill @e1 "bob@test.com"
```

`AGENT_BROWSER_SESSION=myapp` sets the default session for the current shell.

When several sessions share one Chrome over `--cdp <port>`, add `--pin-tab` so each session sticks to its own tab. Every session remembers its bound tab across daemon restarts; with `--pin-tab` a command whose bound tab was closed fails with a `tab_gone` error instead of acting on another session's tab. JSON output includes `"code": "tab_gone"`, `data.targetId`, and an optional sanitized `data.lastUrl` for recovery. Recover with `tab new <url>` or pick a tab from `tab list`. The flag is sticky per session, so pass it once (`--no-pin-tab` turns it off again). See `references/session-management.md` for details.

### Mock network requests

```bash
agent-browser network route "**/api/users" --body '{"users":[]}'   # stub a response
agent-browser network route "**/analytics" --abort                 # block entirely
agent-browser network requests                                     # inspect what fired
agent-browser network har start                                    # record all traffic
# ... perform actions ...
agent-browser network har stop /tmp/trace.har

# HAR files embed text response bodies (JSON/HTML/JS) by default, so the
# recording alone is enough to study a site's API offline. Use
# `--content all` to include binary bodies or `--content none` to disable.
```

### Record a video of the workflow

```bash
agent-browser open https://example.com
agent-browser record start demo.webm
agent-browser snapshot -i
agent-browser click @e3
agent-browser record stop
```

See [references/video-recording.md](references/video-recording.md) for codec options, GIF export, and more.

### Iframes

Iframes are auto-inlined in the snapshot — their refs work transparently:

```bash
agent-browser snapshot -i
# @e3 [Iframe] "payment-frame"
#   @e4 [input] "Card number"
#   @e5 [button] "Pay"

agent-browser fill @e4 "4111111111111111"
agent-browser click @e5
```

To scope a snapshot to an iframe (for focus or deep nesting):

```bash
agent-browser frame @e3      # switch context to the iframe
agent-browser snapshot -i
agent-browser frame main     # back to main frame
```

### Dialogs

`alert` and `beforeunload` are auto-accepted so agents never block. For `confirm` and `prompt`:

```bash
agent-browser dialog status          # is there a pending dialog?
agent-browser dialog accept           # accept
agent-browser dialog accept "text"    # accept with prompt input
agent-browser dialog dismiss          # cancel
```

## Diagnosing install issues

If a command fails unexpectedly (`Unknown command`, `Failed to connect`, stale daemons, version mismatches after `upgrade`, missing Chrome, etc.) run `doctor` before anything else:

```bash
agent-browser doctor                     # full diagnosis (env, Chrome, daemons, config, providers, network, launch test)
agent-browser doctor --offline --quick   # fast, local-only
agent-browser doctor --fix               # also run destructive repairs (reinstall Chrome, purge old state, ...)
agent-browser doctor --json              # structured output for programmatic consumption
```

`doctor` auto-cleans stale socket/pid/version sidecar files on every run. Destructive actions require `--fix`. Exit code is `0` if all checks pass (warnings OK), `1` if any fail.

## Troubleshooting

**"Ref not found" / "Element not found: @eN"** Page changed since the snapshot. Run `agent-browser snapshot -i` again, then use the new refs.

**Element exists in the DOM but not in the snapshot** It's probably off-screen or not yet rendered. Try:

```bash

agent-browser snapshot -i
# or
agent-browser wait --text "..."
agent-browser snapshot -i
```

**Click does nothing / overlay swallows the click** Some modals and cookie banners block other clicks. If `click` reports `covered by <...>`, interact with that covering element first. Otherwise, snapshot, find the dismiss/close button, click it, then re-snapshot.

**Fill / type doesn't work** Some custom input components intercept key events. Try:

```bash
agent-browser focus @e1

# or
agent-browser keyboard type "text"          # raw keystrokes, no selector

**Page needs JS you can't get right in one shot** Use `eval --stdin` with a heredoc instead of inline:

```bash
cat <<'EOF' | agent-browser eval --stdin
// Complex script with quotes, backticks, whatever
document.querySelectorAll('[data-id]').length
EOF
```

Use `frame "#iframe"` to switch into them explicitly if the parent opts in, otherwise the iframe's contents aren't available via snapshot — fall back to `eval` in the iframe's origin or use the `--headers` flag to satisfy CORS.

Relaunch with the `--webgpu` flag, wait for the app's first rendered frame, then screenshot. On Linux install `libvulkan1 mesa-vulkan-drivers` first. Verify with `agent-browser doctor --webgpu`. See [references/webgpu.md](references/webgpu.md).
